en: He sat with hands folded.
What could this dream of mine mean?
Interpret this dream for me,
Before I mount my horse now,
My khan-uncle touched by Kydyr,
Let my uncle Ak Joltoy come,
Tell me what this dream of mine can mean.
He rose, his heart pounding,
His sturdy body trembling,
His thoughts thrown into turmoil,
His breast seemed joined with heaven.
Blood flowed as though dawn were breaking,
The vision appeared before my eyes,
Unable to settle in its place within me,
Was that not my uncle standing there,
My forefather Baibörü, the lion who passed on?
Foremost among the warriors,
He appeared plainly to my true eyes,
This was the lion who blessed me in my dream.
Though stern, my noble elder,
I received what he placed in my hands,
Radiant Ak Joltoy,
Whose support is like a mighty host.
Unlike any ordinary hapless man,
Surely no mere godless fellow,
Unlike the faces of other men,
The warrior moves in splendor,
Towering like a white spear,
How did Artyk interpret it?
Blood flowed and his wrist swelled,
What has happened here?
My fatherly strongman Joltoy,
Interpret this carefully for me.
Hemmed in like a young sapling,
From the course of each dream he had seen,
Appealed to the ancestral spirits:
“Your dream, my son—if such a dream has come—”
To Manas, who dreamed in every sleep,
Reciting the Quran and the sermon,
Reading many days in solemn chant,
Reading all that could inspire wonder,
The hero who returned by the Kongurat road,
The steadfast, noble lion—
If your forefather sent this dream,
With sovereign God above all,
It foretells a rich man granted a child.
His son will be born a warrior,
My dear one, clearly he has granted it.
What your forefather Koshoy bestowed,
He surely bestowed along with it,
A dark-blue warrior, grim as shadow,
Black-chested and blue-backed,
Many stand there without relenting,
All are gathered beyond the ridge,
Leading a vast army that whistles onward,
When he campaigns, he takes the foe,
All his captured spoil is bundled,
A champion set apart from all others,
Where else is there such matchless armor?
Blue-maned one, compose your face,
His throat burned like fire,
Hear his dark and weighty thought,
His bearing remained unwavering,
Excited souls raised a clamor,
The person who heeded his words,
He subdued through entreaty,
The witless man who knew no speech,
He scattered them like upright saplings,
Pleading with the foolish one,
He subdued him by the fangs,
He prized contentment like a nobleman,
His courage flared like a kindled flame,
They learned that he would strike,
He took much while ranging unfulfilled,
He took counsel from the slightest word,
No mortal warrior came against him,
Though wealthy, he did not despise others.
His fortunes stood in perfect balance,
He consoled the one he fixed his gaze upon,
They knew that he would strike;
Your road is exceedingly strong,
May his life be long,
May your guest arrive at little cost.
Kindness will spread among the people,
The child’s fortune will open,
Unburdened by troubles of the eye,
Nothing on earth will remain whole,
A mother’s heart endures forever,
Nothing among the people will remain whole.
Exactly the equal of these men,
Nothing remains whole before God,
Dear Kenen, give it, my child
Go today; do not remain behind
To the words spoken by the stranger
My sacred kinsman, khan elder
Kenen whom you saw, to you
Drawing the sword
It was hero Kenen himself
Taking his whip in hand
My khan elder, the gray wolf
Now be ready for Kenen
Kenen like a falcon
He sent him on the Kalmyk trail
This gift God bestowed
Understand it, my people
Truly sacred Kenen
Kenen, the all-wise one who rises
Why did you go and descend
Kenen, strength of the multitude
May a warrior be granted to sustain life
Grief weighed him down in sorrow
A fighter like a falcon
May he grant a tiger-calf hero
May these words be fitting glad tidings
Trust in the Creator’s protection
May Kenen’s bond be strong
So spoke Ak Joltoy
He said, speak precisely and stand firm
Traveling on without tiring
A host of many kinds advanced
Bertik traveled surely and firmly
From outside, leading the horse
He took it by its muzzle
Taking the forked ridge of the mountain
The mighty champion whom Kozom foretold
When he asked the people for the rope
Looking upon the former misery
This was what they had lacked
Telling what his eyes had seen
The red-eyed one who came to that
Taking burden-bearers by the thousand
Joy filled him like milk
He became a hero to those who came
My sacred eyes found peace
To the peri-born Beybak
Her mouth opened in anguish
When the pain came, the earth groaned
Tears filled both eyes
Uzunkan fell into sorrow
Truly sobbing upon the ground
The messenger ran swiftly
Her cries carried toward Talas
Her dear soul was shaken
Her labor tightened
It bewildered her mind
Her elder’s throat went dry
From the agony and chill
The attendants seized her in distress
Weeping, they begged for help
Pleading to the Creator
Clinging to her tiny life
O Creator, one God
Grant aid to one lying in grievous sorrow
If her life ends, grant her faith
Coming and appearing before their eyes
Without stopping the blue roan
Do not torment her unto death
You brought this upon her in youth
She fell into fierce pain
O Creator of black and dappled things
Pleading to you alone
May there be light beyond her life
Her bones ache and sorrow grows
Her palate dried and her strength departed
Her whole flesh softened
Casting her into care and sorrow
The travail became plain to see
Could they cease making prayers
Her tongue formed its words
Care upon care divided her thoughts
The Uyghur gathered and took the standard
Her soul appeared to flutter
Her watching eyes filled with tears
Sickness gripped all who remained
Saying the living still have strength
What the Creator placed upon her
Let the people hear and know
So the other one spoke
The peri-born Beybak
All the people waited
In the narrowness of her pain
Appearing hateful to the eye
Tears flowed from dear eyes
Bloody, washing her collar
Crying fiercely, gripping her waist
Smoke curled from her mouth
From this fatherless world
She neared the point of not remaining
Those watching gathered around
Standing there without cease
Clinging to poles in anguish
This plea went to God
Pleading to him alone
Her prayer was her only remedy
The dear soul they had found
Truly lay there in travail
Giving strength to her tiny life
The poor soul was filled with worry,
The seventy-year-old dervish Kydyr,
Whose turban was as large as a cauldron,
Whose shout sounded like the call to prayer,
Taking charge of the matter,
He spoke, saying, “Do not grieve,”
Speaking of what he perceived in the child,
The dervish of ninety tribes,
Reciting sacred words four at a time,
When they looked, it was Kydyr himself,
For the unfortunate Perizaada,
The time had come for him to be a firm companion,
Her supporter was Kydyr himself,
A fortunate means and occasion,
The time had come to leave what was bestowed,
The unfortunate Perizaada,
If she did not stray from the path,
The time had come for her protector to depart,
Straining himself over the child,
The time had come to give his blessing;
Saying, “Repent, Bermet, repent,”
Entrusting himself to Providence,
For the unfortunate Kydyr, [?],
He named him [?],
His whole body tingling upward,
Hearing the suddenly uttered command,
A person without an elder brother—oh, elder sister,
This is the deed that remained from then.
The transience of the world,
May he become a shield for the people,
You are the lamb of the Undying One,
Protecting the people when the multitude is thrown into turmoil,
A resounding voice came from the hero,
A sacred voice rang out,
Thus he spoke words about the child,
When they looked, he could not be seen,
No one knew where he was,
Kydyr had bestowed the name,
Their hearts ached, but he was gone,
The man who had spoken these words,
Had vanished from sight.
Kydyr [?],
On the stirring Nights of Power,
The unfortunate Perizaada,
Rose suddenly to her feet,
Before one could say a word,
In the blink of an eye,
While she stood looking at her child,
He vanished from sight,
“As I see it, that is how it was.”
Giving Bermet a blessing,
The time had come for it to settle upon her;
Taking the radiant child,
At the very midpoint [?],
Kydyr parted from them for paradise,
Like dung [?],
Wondrous was the deed wrought by Kydyr,
Dismounting at Makooluk,
The sun shone overhead,
